findings.text: The Overview's "Total" double-counts: `counts()` is given every record task, including ones whose `path` is a folder already listed, and then adds every folder node (`SessionTree.Node.all()` includes the node itself). The draw drops those duplicates but the count keeps them — public/framework/ai/AISession/SessionFeed.js:363 (pass the filtered `own` for the deep count and count unfiltered only for "Own"). The "Total: 471" in live-1920.png is inflated by this.

Older child rows are matched to a session by the parent's name with only a lower time bound, so every `vscode-mastermind` child spawned after 10/20 by ANY later tab counts as e00f55c9's child and adds to its cost — Servex/agents/Agents.js:52-53 (`started_at >= since`, no end). The brief (item 3) asked to map the existing `vscode-mastermind` rows to `e00f55c9`; either bound the match by the next session that used the name, or run the one-off mapping script (dry run + manifest) that the doc defers (core/Session/doc/session-is-a-task.md, last bullet).

Item 4 / Done-when: the session page should show cost and duration computed from the children, but the cost tile still reads "…" in live-1920.png and live-1920-board.png (top band), and the page shows two disagreeing counts ("49 of 83" in the stats bar against "Own tasks: 227" in the feed). Make one count the page's count, or label each one so it says what it counts.

Done-when says the page is "reached from the AI page". review-notes.md (gap 1) says e00f55c9 is in no day's `index.json`, so it opens only by url. That is a miss of the owner's stated check, not just a worktree limit. It can be queued, but the review can't call it met.

Part 3, 12c parts 2–3 (the session names its children in its own record; per-scope `index.jsonl`) are planned in slow-write.md but not built. The write target is met (5–7 ms, slow-write.md table) and the plan is reasonable, but `agents_under` now scans the registry more widely than before (3.3 s cold, slow-write.md), which goes against the owner's "no scan of a global registry".
Part 5 items 21/21b (`Prompt extends Task`, the plainer list name) are not in this diff, and review-notes.md doesn't list them among the deputy's items (it says 1–7, 10–13, 20). Say where they went.

Servex/agents/session_tasks.test.mjs:222 writes a scratch session folder into the live `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/16/` tree. That fires the dev server's watchers, and a crash mid-run leaves a dotted folder behind. It also uses `node:assert`, not `core/Test` as item 11 asks. An OS temp dir (or `Registry`'s `dir`-style override) would be safer.

`Task.List.make` (public/framework/core/Task/Task.js:787) slugs a string to an id but does not check for an existing child with that id. Adding the same title twice in the browser gives two tasks with one id (the item tool checks; the class doesn't).
Simpler: `Task.slug` (Task.js:790) and `slug_of` (Servex/agents/page_tools.js:125) are the same function written twice. page_tools could import `Task.slug` (one of everything, law 6).
In the feed rows the right-hand ▶/■/✓ controls jump between two columns from row to row (live-1920.png, lower band, rows 1–5 against rows 6–8). That is ragged at 1920.

answer.reply: fixed: 2aceb793f. A record task that points at a listed folder is counted once, as the folder. The live shot now reads 232 own and 321 total (it was 471).

fixed: 2aceb793f. An old row (no parent_session) matches by its parent's name only if it started before Agents.NAMES_UNTIL (2026-10-25T06:00Z, after this merge and its restart, when every spawn carries parent_session), so a later tab reusing the name never adds children. No mapping script is needed: before that moment, the name vscode-mastermind was only ever e00f55c9.

fixed (counts) and measured (cost). Each count now says what it counts: '232 tasks of its own · 321 counting subtasks and child sessions' in the feed, 'Task folders done 50 of 83' in the stats bar. The cost tile does fill ($716.76), but it took 64 s on the live Servex, which still runs the read from before this branch (21 s per read in slow-write.md). This branch's read is 1.8 s cold and 56 ms warm; it is re-measured live after the merge and noted in slow-write.md.
